title: PACE%2BCode%2BA%2B2023.pdf — section 18
text:
2.11 There is no power to stop or detain a person in order to find grounds for a search. Police
officers have many encounters with members of the public which do not involve detaining
people against their will and do not require any statutory power for an officer to speak to a
person (see paragraph 4.12 and Note 1). However, if reasonable grounds for suspicion
emerge during such an encounter, the officer may detain the person to search them, even
though no grounds existed when the encounter began. As soon as detention begins, and
before searching, the officer must inform the person that they are being detained for the
purpose of a search and take action in accordance with paragraphs 3.8 to 3.11 under “Steps
to be taken prior to a search”.
(b) Searches authorised under section 60 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994
